clauses.label: Section  1.
clauses.text:
Section  1. Whenever an educational institution submits evidence which satisfies  
the Administrator of Veterans’ Affairs that energy consumption will be abnormally  
high during the winter months or that available energy supplies will be inadequate to  
meet the needs of the school, and that, in the interest of energy conservation, the  
institution plans to close between semesters or terms for a period not to exceed 45 days,  
the Administrator may continue to pay monthly educational assistance benefits to  
veterans and eligible persons enrolled in such schools. Such authority may be exercised  
only once during any 12-month period with respect to any educational institution.

clauses.label: S ec . 2.
clauses.text:
S ec . 2. The Administrator shall advise veterans and other eligible persons of the  
effect of accepting educational assistance benefits under the provisions of Section 1  
of this Order on their period of entitlement.

own_original_text:
Executive Order 12020 November 8, 1977
Payment of Educational Benefits to Veterans and Dependents When Schools  
are Temporarily Closed To Conserve Energy
By virtue of the authority vested in me by clause (A) of Section 1780(a) of Title  
38 of the United States Code, and as President of the United States of America, in  
order to establish a national policy in regard to payment of educational benefits to  
veterans and their dependents during periods in which schools are closed to conserve  
energy, it is hereby ordered as follows:
Section  1. Whenever an educational institution submits evidence which satisfies  
the Administrator of Veterans’ Affairs that energy consumption will be abnormally  
high during the winter months or that available energy supplies will be inadequate to  
meet the needs of the school, and that, in the interest of energy conservation, the  
institution plans to close between semesters or terms for a period not to exceed 45 days,  
the Administrator may continue to pay monthly educational assistance benefits to  
veterans and eligible persons enrolled in such schools. Such authority may be exercised  
only once during any 12-month period with respect to any educational institution.
S ec . 2. The Administrator shall advise veterans and other eligible persons of the  
effect of accepting educational assistance benefits under the provisions of Section 1  
of this Order on their period of entitlement.
T h e W h it e H o u s e,
November 8, 1977.
[FR Doc.77-32768 Filed H-8-77;4:20 pm]

versions.research_rationale:
Read the whole order (42 FR 58509, signed 1977-11-08): section 1 lets the Administrator of Veterans' Affairs continue monthly educational assistance when an institution closes between terms for not more than 45 days to conserve energy, exercisable once in any 12-month period per institution; section 2 requires the Administrator to advise beneficiaries of the effect on their entitlement. The order has no own-terms end. Held current law: the text of 38 U.S.C. 3680 (release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09) now provides in subsection (a)(2)(A) that the Secretary may continue allowances while institutions are temporarily closed under an established policy based on an Executive order of the President or due to an emergency, capped at 4 weeks in any 12-month period, and its note prints this order. The three bounded searches were read against their coverage notes; current-law:usc hits the note, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog have no hit beyond the order. Authority statute checked in force: clause (A) of former section 1780(a), now 38 U.S.C. 3680(a), is in the held text. The 4-week statutory cap and the statute's use of the Secretary are changes made by statute to the underlying authority, not later presidential instruments, and are disclosed in the clause reason.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"No earlier end. The order states no duration or date; the 45-day figure limits each closure, not the order. The later-events:ofr_catalog search has no hit and the bounded search of the held corpus for its number finds only the order's own printing and the 1989 codification. The held 38 U.S.C. 3680(a)(2)(A) refers to an established policy based on an Executive order, which supports continuation rather than an end.","independent_command_check":"Section 2 (advice to veterans about the effect on entitlement) is a duty dependent on section 1 payments and has no separate end; no other independent command appears in the order.","savings_check":"No saving clause. No past payments or entitlements under the order are identified in held sources as surviving independently; state none after bounded search.","scope_check":"One clause (sections 1 and 2 read together). Section 1's authority is now exercised under 38 U.S.C. 3680(a)(2)(A), which names the Secretary of Veterans Affairs and caps continued payment at 4 weeks in any 12-month period; the order's 45-day figure therefore operates only within the statutory 4-week limit. That limit is a statutory narrowing, not an ending of the clause."}

reviews.reasons: Identity, quotes and hashes verify (EO 12020, 1977-11-08, 42 FR 58509; signatory Jimmy Carter per the Code note). The single-scope inventory (sections 1-2) is acceptable and the YES outcome is plausible: 38 U.S.C. 3680(a)(2)(A) still allows continued payment during closures under an established policy based on an Executive order, and the Code prints the order with no ending. But the claim does not date or record the statutory amendment that capped such payments at 4 weeks in any 12-month period (Pub. L. 111-377, effective 2011-08-01), which displaced the order's 45-day term in part, and it wrongly states that clause (A) of former section 1780(a) remains in the held text. Record the 2011 change (and the 2017 re-designation) as later events with date, actor and mechanism.
